scope: How USA Basketball chose its senior men's teams, 2005-2014: appointments, announcement dates, pool sizes, commitment model and stated criteria. Which players were chosen is deliberately not recorded (hindsight for the simulation).
hindsight_gate: Every item carries known_from, the date it became public. The career clock (2004-12-31 when written) must not read an item before its known_from. These are real-world facts; whether the simulated USA Basketball follows them is a simulation decision, not settled by this file.

value.name: Jerry Colangelo
value.title: Managing Director, USA Basketball Men's Senior National Team program

managing_director.note: New position. Responsible for selecting the senior men's coaching staff and players through 2008 and for the teams' preparation (training, exhibitions). Events planned: 2006 World Championship, 2007 FIBA Americas Olympic qualifier if needed, 2008 Olympics if qualified.

sole_selector.value: Colangelo alone was made responsible for selecting the team (replacing the earlier committee approach).

managing_director_2009_2012.value: Colangelo continued, styled USA Basketball chairman, and announced the 2009 camp and 2010-12 pool
managing_director_2009_2012.note: Exact date of his reappointment for 2009-2012 not found.

head_coach_2006_2008.note: Duke Today dates its story 28 Oct 2005; later Duke articles say he was named 26 Oct 2005. Exact day unverified.

assistant_coaches_2006_2008.note: Appointment date not established; in place by the March 2006 pool announcement.

head_coach_2013_2016.note: "In 2013, Team USA announced Krzyzewski would return as head coach from 2013 through 2016."

2006_2008.value: Players were asked for a three-year commitment covering the 2006 World Championship, the 2007 FIBA Americas Olympic qualifier (if needed) and the 2008 Olympics, instead of invitations weeks before a tournament. The pool was fluid: players could be added.

2010_2012.value: Same model: a national team pool for the 2010 World Championship and 2012 Olympics, "fluid" with additions possible; Colangelo cited injuries, family issues and free agency as reasons a strong pool was needed.

2014_2016.value: Initial list of players to be considered for both the 2014 World Cup and the 2016 Olympics

style_of_play.value: "In making the player selections we took into consideration the style of play anticipated to be used by the coaching staff." (Colangelo, 5 Mar 2006)

availability.value: Final rosters were cut from the training-camp finalists after camp; withdrawals for injury, free agency, rest or personal reasons were filled from the pool or by new additions (2010: all ten invited 2008 players declined by early July 2010).

other.note: No published numeric criteria (statistics thresholds, age limits) were found.

pool_announced.note: 18 of the 23 had previously played for USA Basketball. Players were expected to report for training in mid-July 2006.

usa_citizenship.value: A player must hold U.S. nationality (passport) to play for the USA.
usa_citizenship.source: FIBA Internal Regulations Book 3 (Players and Officials), 2020 copy at https://basket.ba/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/FIBA-Internal-Regulations-BOOK-3.pdf; rule quoted in https://jamaicabasketball.org/eligibility
usa_citizenship.note: FIBA eligibility is by legal nationality.

one_naturalised_player.value: A national team in a FIBA competition may have only one player who acquired the nationality of that country by naturalisation or by any other means after reaching 16.
one_naturalised_player.source: FIBA Internal Regulations Book 3 (Players and Officials), 2020 copy at https://basket.ba/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/FIBA-Internal-Regulations-BOOK-3.pdf; rule quoted in https://jamaicabasketball.org/eligibility
one_naturalised_player.note: Wording read from the 2020 Book 3 and secondary sources; the age-16 threshold applied in the 2005-2014 editions was not confirmed from a period copy.

one_country_rule.value: A player who has played for one national team in an official FIBA competition after age 17 may not play for another country (exceptions only by FIBA decision).
one_country_rule.source: FIBA Internal Regulations Book 3 (Players and Officials), 2020 copy at https://basket.ba/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/FIBA-Internal-Regulations-BOOK-3.pdf; rule quoted in https://jamaicabasketball.org/eligibility
one_country_rule.note: Standard FIBA rule; the period wording (age 17, exceptions) was not read from a 2005-2014 copy.

territories.value: Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands have their own FIBA federations; their players are U.S. citizens and may be eligible for either team, subject to the one-country rule.
